Subject: Re: Production errors/timeout spikes on streaming route

Hi Dylan,

We started seeing intermittent stalls and a spike in 500/timeout errors on our ingestion pipeline that uses the Redwood streaming endpoint (route: /v1/stream/generate). The problem began around 07:40 PDT and has affected ~30% of requests — latency jumps to 10-20s and some calls never return.

Attached is a short debug trace from our side (debug_log_0429.txt). We use the official Redwood client SDK (v1.3.2) with chunked transfer encoding on node.

Can you confirm whether there were infra changes or rate-limit throttle events? This is impacting our SLAs — we need a patch or workaround ASAP.

— Samira

Quick triage notes from the infra side (I pulled request traces + worker metrics):
- We see elevated request queues on a subset of GPU workers handling the streaming route between 07:35-08:10 PDT.
- Error surface: connection stalls followed by 502/504 downstream errors. No mass autoscaler events or infra deployments in that window.
- Correlation: a number of stalled requests show a sequence of tiny chunked header frames (0-5 byte header fragments) before body frames. Our runtime accepts them fine, but the SDK's parser seems to treat them as malformed and never completes the stream read on the client side, causing clients to retry or hold connections.

Connor, can you confirm if v1.3.2 had any changes to chunked header parsing?

Samira — attaching a short SLO impact summary (slo_impact_summary_0429.pdf).

[attachment: slo_impact_summary_0429.pdf (application/pdf)]

— Marissa
Sr. SRE, Redwood Inference
From: Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwood.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.ai>
Cc: Samira Khan <samira.k@blueleafanalytics.com>
Date: Thu, 29 Apr 2027 10:26:45 -07:00
Subject: Re: Production errors/timeout spikes on streaming route

Thanks Marissa — I reproduced locally with Blueleaf's repro (thanks Samira). Root cause: an optimization in the Node SDK v1.3.2 that attempted to coalesce chunked header fragments for performance. In certain pathological sequences where small header fragments arrive separated by very short pauses, the parser erroneously awaited more bytes and didn't emit the header-complete event, effectively stalling the stream on the client.

Mitigation options (short-term):
1) Force SDK to fallback to the older header parser via env var REDWOOD_SDK_PARSER=legacy (we can issue a patched release and a temporary tagged build). This unblocks affected customers immediately.
2) Server-side workaround: add a compatibility mode for fragmented headers (adds ~0.5ms overhead per request).

I'll prepare a hotfix PR (hotfix_v1.diff) and a patched npm tag (v1.3.3-compat) in the next 90 minutes. Recommend we ask Blueleaf to switch to the patched client or enable the env var.

— Connor
Lead SDK Engineer, Redwood Inference
